title.from: Static projection publishing: the Markus site as a projection of the content

description.from:
# Static projection publishing: the Markus site as a projection of the content

## Vision (Ryan)
The default publication option for Markus sites is static files in a versioned S3 bucket behind our own CloudFront. The published site is a projection of the content through Markus, not "a build we trigger". The common update is a single-item edit, rendered incrementally and immediately by a Lambda in the GraphQL API path (the existing content-actions custom mutation), writing only the pages that depend on that item. No CodeBuild, no Amplify reader app, no prominent republish button; a full re-projection is an ops maintenance command, like rebuilding a database index. The same GraphQL API's public surface can serve dynamic features on the static pages. Later, an extension/plugin protocol, extracted from a first real plugin.

Design: /Users/home/Projects/markus-publication-architecture-v2.md (v1, superseded direction: markus-publication-architecture.md).

## Measured facts behind it (2026-10-12, see v2 section 1)
- Markus in-process: 2 ms median per page; whole Anth.us site in-process from warm caches is byte-identical (2,352 files) to today's build.
- Cold Anth.us build 283 s locally, 236 s of it image encoding; warm 54 s, 28 s of it one markus subprocess per page.
- content-actions is already a Python 3.12 arm64 zip Lambda (18.5 MB) bundling Markus 0.5.1, Pillow, citeproc; Init 260-345 ms; today's publish takes 1.9-2.8 s (AppSync round trips).

## Decisions already made / constraints
- No CodeBuild, no build job, no Amplify reader app for Markus sites.
- Default publication option for Markus sites = S3 projection (`publication.kind = "s3-projection"`).
- Pre-production sites (Pilobol.us) move fast; Anth.us (production) gets downtime care, parity gates and Ryan's yes per production step.
- Per-site Google projects (unchanged).
- Ryan retires old resources himself (reader apps, buckets, stacks).
- No email addresses in repos (placeholders in specs; allowlists in AWS config).
- Kanbus only through kbs; never edit project/ files by hand.

## Milestones (epics, in dependency order)
M0 spike, M1 projection core + template option, M2 renditions at upload, M3 incremental dependents + reconcile, M4 cache strategy, M5 Pilobol.us migration, M6 Anth.us migration, M7 retire reader apps + template cleanup, M8 public surface, M9 first plugin -> extension protocol, M10 docs + README diagram.

Related (not children): PPY-1f1489 (four-site alignment), PPY-7d8cd0 (Phase 6 moves).
description.to:
# Markus for everything

Latest organizing decision approved by Ryan: this EXISTING initiative is the umbrella for one editable Markus page/content system across homepage `/`, product pages such as `/features` and documentation/wiki subtrees such as `/wiki`; reusable includes and their generated dependency index; post-save incremental public projection; both RSS and Atom; minimal versioned headless delivery; and relevant shared Help/documentation. “Wiki” is navigation/presentation over ordinary content, not a second storage or publishing engine. “Include” is the working name; exact syntax, extension ownership and path/selection schemas remain design decisions. No new initiative or duplicate site/wiki system is created.

Existing static projection publishing, its milestones, implementation evidence and migration history are retained below as supporting scope. Reuse the current content lifecycle and projection/invalidation machinery; new architecture does not authorize a custom-Python content-assembly shortcut. Anth.us-web's current custom Python homepage assembly is a documented migration starting point, not the target. Theme-owned outer chrome and current routes/content/SEO/brand parity are required. RSS/Atom is now a slice of this shared architecture, not a standalone low-hanging-fruit alternative. Incremental vertical slices are welcome when they develop the agreed reusable authored-page/include primitives and shared selection/metadata; no implementation has been authorized for these new plans.

Hierarchy: foundation epic PPY-3f55c3 owns unified-page, authored composition/include, post-save and include-documentation behaviors; delivery epics PPY-33854a and PPY-29da48 retain their foundation/post-save dependencies; Help/docs epic PPY-9ad680 is now a child here; existing all-sites epic PPY-e315d3 retains Anth.us migration design and prior product migration records. Monitoring PPY-2d77c8 stays separate and is only related to this initiative, with no invented blocking dependency. Core foundation/page/include/post-save and both delivery epics are high-priority planning; Help/docs remains supporting medium-priority work. Prioritization is not coding, migration, publication or deployment authorization.

## Preserved static-projection scope and history
